items.stem: Why does partitioning data enable a distributed engine to run faster?

options.text: Partitions can be processed in parallel across many nodes
options.rationale: Correct: independent partitions allow parallel computation.

options.text: Partitioning compresses the data to zero
options.rationale: Partitioning splits data; it does not eliminate it.

options.text: It removes the need for any computation
options.rationale: Computation still happens, just in parallel.
Partitioning is unrelated to data quality.

items.explanation: Correct: independent partitions allow parallel computation.

items.stem: Which TWO are true about a lakehouse compared with a raw data lake? (Select TWO.)

options.text: It adds schema, transactions and governance on top of lake storage
options.rationale: Correct: open table formats bring warehouse-like features to the lake.

options.text: It can support both BI queries and large-scale processing
options.rationale: Correct: a lakehouse aims to serve both workloads.

options.text: It removes the ability to store raw files
options.rationale: A lakehouse still stores files; it adds structure over them.

options.text: It requires abandoning all open formats
options.rationale: Lakehouses are built on open table formats.

items.explanation: Correct: open table formats bring warehouse-like features to the lake.

items.stem: A requirement needs results within seconds of each event arriving. Which approach fits?

options.rationale: Correct: low-latency per-event results call for streaming.
Nightly batch cannot deliver second-level latency.
Manual exports are not continuous or timely.
That cannot meet a seconds-latency requirement.

items.explanation: Correct: low-latency per-event results call for streaming.
